To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Viola-Jone’s face detection framework is a very efficient and reliable method for face detection, that the OpenCV’s public domain classifiers are not the most suitable ones, and that a simple combination of the most suitable classifiers is able to increase the facial detection rate.
(i) The best public domain classifier for face detection achieves 0.97 recall at 0.03 false positives per image.

the best public domain Haar detectors for face detection are the frontal face and profile face classifiers, and the best Haar detectors for facial feature detection are the eye and the nose classifiers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evaluation and comparison of the performance of public Haar-based classifiers for face and facial feature object detection.
the performance analysis of the public domain face and facial feature detectors, the combination of those classifiers and the definition of a new baseline.
the evaluation of a collection of public classifiers, their combination and the definition of a new baseline to be used for future approaches.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the public domain Viola-Jones face classifiers are a good baseline for face detection, but the public domain Violas-Jones classifiers for facial feature detection are not good enough to use as a baseline.
, in general, Viola-Jones based face detection approaches are not reliable in the presence of cluttered background.

the best performance for the facial feature detection task is achieved by the combination of the classifiers for eye, nose and mouth, while the best performance for face detection is obtained by the combination of classifiers for face and eye.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present the best performance for face and facial feature public domain Haar classifiers, as well as the best performance for a hierarchical combination of those public domain classifiers.
we have provided a baseline for the performance of the public domain classifiers, as well as a new method to increase the facial features detection rate.
we have evaluated the performance of all public domain classifiers for face and facial feature (eye, mouth, nose) detection, and we have defined a baseline to compare new approaches.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Viola-Jone's approach is not the best option for facial feature detection.
the performance of these public detectors is not as good as it was expected.
the public domain classifiers are not as accurate and robust as the state of the art approaches.
